newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Analysts budget forecasts too optimistic - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Analysts budget forecasts too optimistic - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Sunday analysts forecasting a better than expected budget deficit for the year to June 30, 1998 were being too optimistic.

Access Economics, which produces Australia's most detailed private fiscal estimates, said in its annual budget preview last week that government finances were in better condition than shown in official estimates and that the 1997/98 budget deficit should be lower than expected.
Access forecast an underlying budget deficit starting point of A$2.6 billion before any further budget cuts are implemented.
"Access gave a very optimistic forecast. I wish they were right but, unhappily, they weren't," Costello told the Nine Network's Sunday programme.
Costello is due to announce the government's budget for the year to June 30, 1998 next Tuesday at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).

The latest government budget estimates, released in January, said current fiscal policies would produce an underlying deficit, which excludes asset sales, of A$3.9 billion for the year to June 1998 and A$2.2 billion the following year.
The government's current fiscal target is to eliminate the deficit for 1998/99.
Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the government to announce an A$2 billion underlying deficit for 1997/98, compared with an estimated underlying deficit of around A$8.5 billion in 1996/97.
The economist saw little challenge in the government cutting the 1997/98 budget by A$2 billion, compared with the A$7 billion cuts for the same fiscal year projected in last year's budget.
Costello said on Sunday the government had broken the back of the $10 billion budget deficit, but that there was still a big task ahead.
"We'll need to consolidate and extend the work that we began in August of last year," he said.
Costello also ruled out speculation that it could reach an underlying budget balance a year earlier than expected.
"Oh, we wish that the speculators were informed," he said.
